title: fix(test): fix hash is not stable on Windows
author: cscnk52
summary: Normalizes backslashes to `/` before hashing the source path for CSS module class names, and also drops the `path.is_absolute()` guard so relative paths are diffed against project_root too. Titled as a test fix, but it changes generated class names for real users.
evidence: Master src/css_modules.rs still hashes `source.to_string_lossy()` unnormalized, so Windows and POSIX produce different hashes for the same project. The change alters every hashed class name for Windows users (and for relative-path inputs with a relative project_root on all platforms), i.e. a breaking output change for CSS modules consumers with persisted class names / SSR caches. #1120 (same root cause, open, also by a contributor) does the same normalization plus string-prefix stripping for relative paths. No maintainer comments on either.
decision: Should CSS module hashes be made platform-independent (changing every hashed class name on Windows) in a minor release, and if so via #1247's minimal change or #1120's broader one?
